jobs.title: Schnupperlehre Polymechaniker/in EFZ
jobs.description:
An der Universität Bern werden jährlich drei Lehrstellen als Polymechaniker/in EFZ neu besetzt. Die Ausbildung wird an den drei Instituten Physikalisches Institut, ARTORG und DCBP angeboten.
Ausbildung
Während der ersten Lehrhälfte wird in der Grundausbildung ein breites Fundament an Wissen und Können gelegt. In der Werkstatt werden Arbeitstechniken wie manuelle und maschinelle Fertigungstechnik, Montagetechnik, Fügetechnik, Wartung und fachspezifische Arbeitssicherheit vermittelt. In der erweiterten Grundausbildung werden die verschiedenen Arbeitstechniken durch exemplarisches Lernen an und Projekten vertieft. Die Schwerpunktausbildung erfolgt in der zweiten Lehrhälfte. In dieser Ausbildungsphase wird die Bedienung und Programmierung von CNC-gesteuerten Werkzeugmaschinen vermittelt. In einem Konstruktionspraktikum erfolgt der Einblick in die Konstruktions- und CAD-Technik.
Die 
• Anforderungen
Gesucht werden motivierte, gute Sekundar- oder sehr gute Realschüler/innen mit sehr guten Kenntnissen in Mathematik und Physik. Zudem sind Interesse an technischen Zusammenhängen, handwerkliches Geschick, gutes räumliches Vorstellungsvermögen sowie eine exakte und selbständige Arbeitsweise gefragt. Ausdauer, Durchhaltevermögen, Geduld und Zuverlässigkeit sindebenso wichtige Eigenschaften. Der Beruf bedingt, dass du frei von Allergien auf Metalle, Öle und Fette bist.
Die Schnupperlehre
Die Schnupperlehre bietet dir die Möglichkeit, den Beruf des Polymechanikers sowie die Institute ARTORG, DCBP und das Physikalische Institut näher kennenzulernen und erste Erfahrungen in der Arbeitswelt zu sammeln. Die Schnupperlehre wird von Januar bis Juni, jeweils von Montag bis Mittwoch, angeboten.
Bewerbungen für eine Schnupperlehre

descriptionByLocale.it:
I tre istituti dell'Istituto di Fisica, ARTORG e DCBP offrono la formazione. Compiti: Durante la prima metà del corso, si pone un'ampia base sulle conoscenze e sulle competenze. In officina vengono insegnate tecniche di lavoro come la tecnologia di fabbricazione manuale e meccanica, la tecnologia di assemblaggio, l'unione di tecnologia, la manutenzione e la sicurezza specialistica. Nella formazione di base estesa, le varie tecniche di lavoro sono approfondite da ex-studi e progetti. La formazione principale è nella seconda metà dell'apprendistato. Durante questa fase di formazione, il funzionamento e la programmazione di macchine utensili controllati CNC è insegnato. In uno stage di progettazione, la comprensione del design e la tecnologia CAD è fornita.
• Requisiti: Motivated, buon Sekundar o molto buoni studenti reali con una buona conoscenza della matematica e della fisica sono ricercati. Inoltre, l'interesse per i rapporti tecnici, l'artigianalità, la buona immaginazione spaziale e un metodo di lavoro preciso e indipendente sono necessarie. Perseveranza, perseveranza, pazienza e affidabilità sono anche caratteristiche importanti. La professione richiede che tu sia privo di allergie ai metalli, oli e grassi.
• Offriamo: L'apprendistato ti offre l'opportunità di conoscere la professione di polimeccanica così come gli istituti ARTORG, DCBP e il physikalische Institut e di acquisire le prime esperienze nel mondo del lavoro. L'apprendistato è offerto da gennaio a giugno, da lunedì a mercoledì.
descriptionByLocale.en:
The three institutes of the Institute of Physics, ARTORG and DCBP offer the training. Tasks: During the first half of the course, a broad foundation is laid on knowledge and skills. In the workshop, work techniques such as manual and machine manufacturing technology, assembly technology, joining technology, maintenance and specialist safety are taught. In the extended basic training, the various working techniques are deepened by ex-studies and projects. The main training is in the second half of the apprenticeship. During this training phase, the operation and programming of CNC-controlled machine tools is taught. In a design internship, the insight into the design and CAD technology is provided.
• Requirements: Motivated, good Sekundar or very good real students with very good knowledge of mathematics and physics are sought. In addition, interest in technical relationships, craftsmanship, good spatial imagination and an exact and independent working method are required. Perseverance, perseverance, patience and reliability are also important characteristics. The profession requires that you are free of allergies to metals, oils and fats.
• We offer: The apprenticeship offers you the opportunity to get to know the profession of polymechanics as well as the institutes ARTORG, DCBP and the Physikalische Institut and to gain first experiences in the world of work. The apprenticeship is offered from January to June, from Monday to Wednesday.

descriptionByLocale.fr:
À l'Université de Berne, trois apprentissages sont remplis chaque année en tant que polymécanicien/en EFZ. La formation est offerte dans les trois instituts de physique, ARTORG et DCBP.
Formation
Au cours de la première moitié de l'enseignement, un large socle de connaissances et de compétences est posé dans la formation de base. Au cours de l'atelier, des techniques de travail telles que la technologie de production manuelle et mécanique, la technologie d'assemblage, la technologie d'assemblage, la maintenance et la sécurité au travail spécifique sont enseignées. Dans le cadre de la formation de base étendue, les différentes techniques de travail sont approfondies par des apprentissages et des projets exemplaires. La formation ciblée a lieu dans la seconde moitié de l'enseignement. Dans cette phase de formation, on enseigne le fonctionnement et la programmation des machines-outils contrôlées par CNC. Dans le cadre d'un stage de conception, la connaissance de la conception et de la technologie CAO a lieu.
Les
• Exigences
Nous sommes à la recherche d'étudiants motivés, bon secondaire ou très bon réel avec de très bonnes connaissances en mathématiques et en physique. De plus, il faut s'intéresser aux connexions techniques, à l'artisanat, à une bonne imagination spatiale et à une méthode de travail exacte et indépendante. L'endurance, la persévérance, la patience et la fiabilité sont des caractéristiques tout aussi importantes. La profession exige que vous soyez exempts d'allergies aux métaux, aux huiles et aux graisses.
La théorie du procès
L'apprentissage d'essai vous offre la possibilité de connaître la profession de polymécanique ainsi que les instituts ARTORG, DCBP et l'Institut physique et d'acquérir une expérience initiale dans le monde du travail. L'apprentissage d'essai est offert de janvier à juin, du lundi au mercredi.

jobs.description:
UniBE is prestigious.
With us, you benefit from the excellent reputation of a long-standing institution all around the world.

## The project
is funded by the SNSF and the DFG in the framework of the CSCS research unit. In grass leaves, stomatal rows always form next to leaf veins, suggesting that this spatial coordination is important for water supply and demand (Baird & Raissig (2026) Ann Rev Plant Biol Ann Rev Plant Biol). Yet how the development of veins and stomata is spatially coordinated remains an open question. Building on a single-cell atlas of grass leaf development from the first phase of this research unit (Berg et al. (2026) Plant Cell), this project will use spatial genomics, imaging, genetics and biochemistry to uncover how these two tissues communicate to place stomatal rows robustly next to the leaf veins.

## 
• We offer
a vibrant and inclusive research environment that strives to answer fundamental questions in plant development and physiology of grasses and succulents (see our lab mission statement). 
• We offer state-of-the-art research infrastructure at the Institute of Plant Sciences in Bern, Switzerland (http://www.ips.unibe.ch). We are also affiliated with the Microscope Imaging Centre (www.mic.unibe.ch) and the Oeschger Centre for Climate Change Research (www.oeschger.unibe.ch). This project is part of the Research Unit “Cereal Stem Cell Systems” (https://cerealstemcells.de).
Strong research infrastructure and international network
Application and Contact
To apply, please send a single PDF including a motivation letter, a CV, and the names of at least two referees to michael.raissig@unibe.ch. The start date of the position is flexible. We start reviewing applications on September 14th, 2026, until the position is filled.
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About us
The “Stomatal Biology” group is welcoming applications for a fully funded post-doctoral position (2 years, extension possible). Our group studies how grasses and succulents build and pattern their 'breathing pores' or stomata by combining single-cell genomics, live imaging, genetics and protein biochemistry. We are hosted at the Institute of Plant Sciences, University of Bern, and work at the intersection of plant developmental genetics, cell biology and gas-exchange physiology. Within the research unit “Cereal Stem Cell Systems - RU52350; https://cerealstemcells.de”, we are recruiting a Postdoc to investigate how grass leaves spatially coordinate the development of their veins and stomata.
We are looking for a postdoc with a completed PhD in plant biology, developmental biology, molecular biology or a related field. Proficient written and oral English skills and solid experience in (plant) molecular genetics, microscopy, and cell biology are required. Previous experience with model grass species, (plant) signalling, protein biochemistry, or single-cell/spatial transcriptomics is an advantage. An open, collaborative mindset for working within the research unit is expected.

Aufgaben:
è finanziato dal SNSF e dal DFG nel quadro dell'unità di ricerca CSCS. Nelle foglie di erba, le file stomatiche si formano sempre accanto alle venature fogliari, suggerendo che questo coordinamento spaziale è importante per l'offerta e la domanda di acqua (Baird & Raissig (2026) Ann Rev Plant Biol Ann Rev Plant Biol). Tuttavia, come lo sviluppo delle vene e degli stomi sia strutturalmente coordinato rimane una domanda aperta. Costruire su un atlante monocellulare dello sviluppo di foglie di erba dalla prima fase di questa unità di ricerca (Berg et al. a vibrant and inclusive research environment that strives to answer fundamental questions in plant development and physiology of grasses and succulents (see our lab mission statement).

With us, you create value.

## About us
The “Stomatal Biology” group is welcoming applications for a fully funded post-doctoral position (2 years, extension possible). Our group studies how grasses and succulents build and pattern their 'breathing pores' or stomata by combining single-cell genomics, live imaging, genetics and protein biochemistry. We are hosted at the Institute of Plant Sciences, University of Bern, and work at the intersection of plant developmental genetics, cell biology and gas-exchange physiology. Within the research unit “Cereal Stem Cell Systems - RU52350; https://cerealstemcells.de”, we are recruiting a Postdoc to investigate how grass leaves spatially coordinate the development of their veins and stomata.
We are looking for a postdoc with a completed PhD in plant biology, developmental biology, molecular biology or a related field. Proficient written and oral English skills and solid experience in (plant) molecular genetics, microscopy, and cell biology are required. Previous experience with model grass species, (plant) signalling, protein biochemistry, or single-cell/spatial transcriptomics is an advantage. An open, collaborative mindset for working within the research unit is expected.

UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## What You Can Expect
You will join an active, supportive, inclusive, and collaborative research environment at the Department of Mathematics and Statistics. You will work on exciting fundamental questions at the interface of mathematics and modern AI and collaborate with national and international researchers. You will also contribute to teaching as a teaching assistant.
Employment conditions and remuneration are in accordance with the standards of the University of Bern, Switzerland.

## Profile of the Candidate
Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a Master's degree in pure or applied mathematics, theoretical physics, statistics, or a related field.
We seek motivated candidates with a strong background in mathematics (e.g., in one or more of the following areas: analysis, probability theory, stochastic processes, statistical physics, optimal transport, dynamical systems, optimization, or machine learning theory), an interest in the mathematical principles underlying modern AI (or in related problems), the ability to work both independently and collaboratively, and good written and spoken English. Knowledge of German is not required. Programming experience is beneficial but not required.
International reputation
Application and Contact
Applications should include:
• a motivation letter (maximum one page);
• a curriculum vitae (maximum two pages);
• available BSc/MSc diplomas or academic transcripts;
• the names and contact details of one or two referees; and
• optional: a summary of the master's thesis (maximum two pages)
Review of applications will begin in the last week of August 2026 and continue until the position is filled. The earliest possible starting date is October 2026. The exact starting date will be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

## About the Project
Modern artificial intelligence systems achieve remarkable performance, yet the mathematical mechanisms underlying their behavior remain only partially understood. This project seeks to develop a rigorous theory of modern learning algorithms and to explain how their architecture and dynamics determine their performance.
Depending on their background and interests, the candidate will use tools from analysis, probability theory, stochastic processes, statistical physics, dynamical systems, optimization, and optimal transport to prove mathematical results describing the behavior of modern learning algorithms in suitable abstract settings. Possible research directions include training dynamics and signal propagation in deep neural networks, including transformers; generative modeling; high-dimensional learning systems; sampling algorithms; collective phenomena in large-scale models; and quantum algorithms.
The work will be primarily theoretical. Computational experiments may be used to guide conjectures and illustrate theoretical results, depending on the candidate's interests.
What You Can Expect

jobs.description:
UniBE is interconnected.
With us, you're part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary collaboration.

## Scope of this position
The successful candidate will focus on the training in morphological pathology of farm, companion & zoo animals during the first year, which can also account for an internship. At the end of the first year, we will jointly evaluate the candidate's interests and career goals. The training can then continue along one of two pathways:
• Residency in Veterinary Anatomic Pathology – up to three additional years of structured diagnostic training and preparation for the board examination of the European College of Veterinary Pathologists (ECVP); or
• Combined Residency/PhD Program – integrating pathology residency training with an intensive research program leading to a PhD through the Graduate School for Cellular and Biomedical Sciences at the University of Bern (six-year appointment).
Both pathways provide structured preparation for the ECVP board examination. Candidates pursuing the combined Residency/PhD program will have the opportunity to conduct research in areas including cancer therapy resistance, DNA repair, and host–pathogen interactions within the collaborative research environment of the University of Bern.
More information about the Institute of Animal Pathology and its training and research programs is available on our website Institute of Animal Pathology.

## Your profile
We are looking for a highly motivated veterinarian with a strong interest in pathology and research. The following qualifications are required:
• a degree in veterinary medicine (Master of Veterinary Medicine, DVM, or equivalent);
• a collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for contributing to our team-based approach to diagnostics, teaching, and research;
• fluency in English and German language skills at a minimum B2 level at the time of the interview.
• Fluency in French is not required but is considered an advantage.
We offer an enthusiastic diagnostic team, an inspiring research environment, excellent research training in cancer therapy resistance, DNA repair, and host–pathogen interactions, long-standing experience in preparing candidates for the ECVP board examination, and an attractive working environment in Bern. Remuneration is in accordance with the regulations of the University of Bern.

descriptionByLocale.en:
UniBE is interconnected.
With us, you're part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary collaboration.

## Scope of this position
The successful candidate will focus on the training in morphological pathology of farm, companion & zoo animals during the first year, which can also account for an internship. At the end of the first year, we will jointly evaluate the candidate's interests and career goals. The training can then continue along one of two pathways:
• Residency in Veterinary Anatomic Pathology – up to three additional years of structured diagnostic training and preparation for the board examination of the European College of Veterinary Pathologists (ECVP); or
• Combined Residency/PhD Program – integrating pathology residency training with an intensive research program leading to a PhD through the Graduate School for Cellular and Biomedical Sciences at the University of Bern (six-year appointment).
Both pathways provide structured preparation for the ECVP board examination. Candidates pursuing the combined Residency/PhD program will have the opportunity to conduct research in areas including cancer therapy resistance, DNA repair, and host–pathogen interactions within the collaborative research environment of the University of Bern.
More information about the Institute of Animal Pathology and its training and research programs is available on our website Institute of Animal Pathology.

## Your profile
We are looking for a highly motivated veterinarian with a strong interest in pathology and research. The following qualifications are required:
• a degree in veterinary medicine (Master of Veterinary Medicine, DVM, or equivalent);
• a collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for contributing to our team-based approach to diagnostics, teaching, and research;
• fluency in English and German language skills at a minimum B2 level at the time of the interview.
• Fluency in French is not required but is considered an advantage.
We offer an enthusiastic diagnostic team, an inspiring research environment, excellent research training in cancer therapy resistance, DNA repair, and host–pathogen interactions, long-standing experience in preparing candidates for the ECVP board examination, and an attractive working environment in Bern. Remuneration is in accordance with the regulations of the University of Bern.

jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## Tasks
Your focus will be on the concept of hardware and software development of PLC Systems, in particular in the context of an adaptive optics real-time system for a ground-based telescope.
The position comprises following tasks:
• Electrical concept and system definition, including the design of electrical schematics
• System and subsystem preparation, assembly, and cabling
• System and Sub-system programming on PLC System (Beckhoff)
• Interface programming for testing and script development (Python)
• System and Sub-system, hardware integration, testing, verification and validation
• Creating and maintaining the required documentation

## Requirements
• Automation Technician (Automatiker) HF/FH or equivalent engineering B.Sc.
• Experience in programming Beckhoff PLCs and developing test scripts using Python.
• Experience in C/C++ software development would be an advantage.
• Good spoken and written knowledge of English is required. German would be an advantage.
International reputation
Application and Contact
Please upload your application via the red button "apply" IN ONE PDF DOCUMENT including the following documents:
• CV (in months/years)
• Cover letter (maximum 1 page)
• Relevant diplomas / certificates
• Relevant supporting documents
Application deadline: 30.09.2026
Incomplete applications will neither be confirmed nor considered.
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About us
The Space Research and Planetology Division at the University of Bern researches the formation and evolution of our solar system. For this purpose, among other things, highly specialized instruments are developed and built for spacecraft, which subsequently carry out measurements in situ, e.g. in the vicinity of Jupiter. Our team is internationally recognized for its achievements and cooperates in numerous space missions, with, for example, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the American space agency, NASA. On top of space-related activities, our Division is also involved in flagship projects for ground-based astronomy, such as for the European 39-m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). In this context, we were recently awarded funding to develop an adaptive optics (AO) system for the 80-cm telescope of the Zimmerwald Observatory, in collaboration with the Astronomical Institute of the University of Bern (AIUB) and EPFL. To help meet these challenges, we are now seeking an experienced Automation Technician (Automatiker) HF/FH.
The position is available starting soon, or upon negotiation, for an initial period of one year with the option of extension. Our salary range is determined in accordance with the personnel regulations of the Canton of Bern.

With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## Tasks
Your focus will be on the concept of hardware and software development of PLC Systems, in particular in the context of an adaptive optics real-time system for a ground-based telescope.
The position comprises following tasks:
• Electrical concept and system definition, including the design of electrical schematics
• System and subsystem preparation, assembly, and cabling
• System and Sub-system programming on PLC System (Beckhoff)
• Interface programming for testing and script development (Python)
• System and Sub-system, hardware integration, testing, verification and validation
• Creating and maintaining the required documentation

## Requirements
• Automation Technician (Automatiker) HF/FH or equivalent engineering B.Sc.
• Experience in programming Beckhoff PLCs and developing test scripts using Python.
• Experience in C/C++ software development would be an advantage.
• Good spoken and written knowledge of English is required. German would be an advantage.

## About us
The Space Research and Planetology Division at the University of Bern researches the formation and evolution of our solar system. For this purpose, among other things, highly specialized instruments are developed and built for spacecraft, which subsequently carry out measurements in situ, e.g. in the vicinity of Jupiter. Our team is internationally recognized for its achievements and cooperates in numerous space missions, with, for example, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the American space agency, NASA. On top of space-related activities, our Division is also involved in flagship projects for ground-based astronomy, such as for the European 39-m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). In this context, we were recently awarded funding to develop an adaptive optics (AO) system for the 80-cm telescope of the Zimmerwald Observatory, in collaboration with the Astronomical Institute of the University of Bern (AIUB) and EPFL. To help meet these challenges, we are now seeking an experienced Automation Technician (Automatiker) HF/FH.
The position is available starting soon, or upon negotiation, for an initial period of one year with the option of extension. Our salary range is determined in accordance with the personnel regulations of the Canton of Bern.

jobs.description:
UniBE is quintessentially Bernese.
With us, you can expect a culture of respect and a healthy working environment.

## 
• Your profile
We are seeking an internationally recognized individual with proven clinical expertise in palliative medicine, as well as experience in leading clinical structures and interprofessional teams. The future appointee is expected to strategically develop the University Center for Palliative Care, strengthen the integration of palliative medicine across clinical disciplines, and actively contribute to regional and supra-regional networking in palliative care.
Applicants are expected to have an independent and internationally visible research profile, demonstrated by regular publications and successful acquisition of competitive third-party funding. The successful candidate will further expand research in palliative medicine, particularly in health services research and interdisciplinary collaborations, and contribute to the national and international positioning of Bern as a center of excellence.
A strong commitment to undergraduate teaching, as well as to the education, training, and continuing professional development of healthcare professionals, is required. This includes the advancement of palliative care curricula in medical education, the promotion of interprofessional training formats, and active support of early-career researchers.
Requirements include a habilitation or an equivalent academic qualification, as well as board certification with a specialization (SIWF/FMH) in palliative medicine. Additional qualifications, for example in management or organizational development, are considered an advantage.
As an integrative and trustworthy personality, you possess strong communication and team-building skills. You promote interprofessional collaboration, integrate diverse perspectives, and actively engage in cooperation with regional and national partner institutions. You are also committed to fostering an open and respectful work environment and to promoting equality and diversity.

## Self-conception
The University of Bern aims to increase the proportion of women in teaching and research and therefore explicitly encourages qualified female scientists to apply. The University offers various measures to support work–life balance, including childcare services and partner support programs (https://www.vereinbarkeit.unibe.ch/index_eng.html). Job-sharing applications are welcome.
International reputation
Application and Contact
Applications must be submitted solely electronically no later than 2 October 2026 to the Dean's Office of the Medical Faculty of the University of Bern by this link
https://www.recruiting.medizin.unibe.ch/position/14352388
Further information regarding required documentation can be found under https://www.medizin.unibe.ch/research/academic_career_paths/professorship/index_eng.html#pane1397223
or under https://kdrive.medicinebern.ch/app/share/991093/bc77beab-f75a-4634-bbeb-487240307ec0
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About us
The University Center for Palliative Care (UZP) is an interdisciplinary cross-sectional unit at Inselspital and a central academic structure for specialized palliative care, clinical research, and teaching. The Center provides comprehensive medical, nursing, and psychosocial care for patients with complex, advanced, or incurable diseases. In addition to inpatient services, it offers specialized outpatient care and a consultation service within the university hospital. A particular focus lies on interprofessional care, the early integration of palliative expertise in complex disease trajectories, and the further development of evidence-based, patient-centered care models.

Aufgaben:
Siamo alla ricerca di un individuo riconosciuto a livello internazionale con comprovata esperienza clinica in medicina palliativa, nonché esperienza nelle principali strutture cliniche e team interprofessionali. Il futuro candidato dovrebbe sviluppare strategicamente il Centro Universitario per la Cura Palliativa, rafforzare l'integrazione della medicina palliativa attraverso le discipline cliniche, e contribuire attivamente alla rete regionale e sopraregionale in assistenza palliativa.

I candidati dovrebbero avere un profilo di ricerca indipendente e visibile a livello internazionale, dimostrato da pubblicazioni regolari e l'acquisizione di un finanziamento competitivo di terzi. Il candidato di successo amplierà ulteriormente la ricerca in medicina palliativa, in particolare nella ricerca di servizi sanitari e collaborazioni interdisciplinari, e contribuirà al posizionamento nazionale e internazionale di Berna come centro di eccellenza.

È richiesto un forte impegno per l'insegnamento universitario, così come per l'istruzione, la formazione e lo sviluppo professionale continua di professionisti sanitari. Questo include l'avanzamento dei curricula di assistenza palliativa nell'educazione medica, la promozione dei formati di formazione interprofessionale, e il supporto attivo dei ricercatori di pronto soccorso.

I requisiti includono una abilitazione o una qualifica accademica equivalente, così come la certificazione di bordo con una specializzazione (SIWF/FMH) in medicina palliativa. Le qualifiche aggiuntive, ad esempio nella gestione o nello sviluppo organizzativo, sono considerate un vantaggio.

Come personalità integrativa e affidabile, possiedi forti capacità di comunicazione e di team building. Promuovete la collaborazione interprofessionale, integrate diverse prospettive e impegnate attivamente in collaborazione con le istituzioni partner regionali e nazionali. Ti impegni anche a promuovere un ambiente di lavoro aperto e rispettoso e a promuovere l'uguaglianza e la diversità.

Anforderungen:
L'Università di Berna mira ad aumentare la percentuale di donne nell'insegnamento e nella ricerca e quindi incoraggia esplicitamente l'applicazione di scienziati femminili qualificati. L'Università offre varie misure per sostenere l'equilibrio tra lavoro e vita, compresi i servizi di assistenza all'infanzia e i programmi di sostegno ai partner (https://www.vereinbarkeit.unibe.ch/index eng.html). Le applicazioni di condivisione del lavoro sono benvenute.

Gesucht wird eine international anerkannte Persönlichkeit mit ausgewiesener klinischer Expertise in der Palliativmedizin sowie mit Erfahrung in der Leitung klinischer Strukturen und interprofessioneller Teams. Die zukünftige Stelleninhaberin bzw. der zukünftige Stelleninhaber soll das Universitäre Zentrum für Palliative Care strategisch weiterentwickeln, die Integration palliativmedizinischer Kompetenzen in unterschiedliche klinische Fachdisziplinen stärken und die regionale sowie überregionale Vernetzung der Palliative Care aktiv mitgestalten.
Erwartet wird ein eigenständiges, international sichtbares wissenschaftliches Profil mit regelmässiger Publikationstätigkeit sowie erfolgreicher Einwerbung kompetitiver Drittmittel. Die zukünftige Stelleninhaberin bzw. der zukünftige Stelleninhaber soll die Forschung im Bereich der Palliativmedizin, insbesondere in der Versorgungsforschung sowie in interdisziplinären Forschungskooperationen, weiter ausbauen und zur nationalen und internationalen Positionierung des Standorts Bern beitragen.
Ein starkes Engagement in der studentischen Lehre sowie in der Aus-, Weiter- und Fortbildung von Gesundheitsfachpersonen wird vorausgesetzt. An independent, internationally visible scientific profile with regular publication activity and successful acquisition of competitive third-party funding is expected. The future position holder is to further expand research in the field of palliative medicine, in particular in health care research and in interdisciplinary research cooperations, and contribute to the national and international positioning of the Berne location. A strong commitment in student teaching as well as in the education, further and further education of health professionals is required. This includes the further development of palliative medicine teaching content in medical studies as well as the promotion of interprofessional training formats and the active support of young scientists. A habilitation or an equivalent academic track record as well as a specialist title with a focus on SIWF/FMH in the field of palliative medicine are required. Additional qualifications, for example in management or organizational development, are beneficial. As an integrative and confidence-building personality, you have strong communicative and team-building skills. They promote interprofessional cooperation, integrate different perspectives and are actively involved in cooperation with regional and national partner institutions. jobs.description:
UniBE is quintessentially Bernese.
With us, you can expect a culture of respect and a healthy working environment.

## 
• Your profile
The successful candidate will be responsible for establishing an independent research program in neuromorphic systems, with the goal of securing external funding and promoting interdisciplinary collaboration. This includes collaboration within the Faculty of Medicine – such as with the Institute of Physiology, the Center for Experimental Neurology (ZEN), the Neuroengineering Technologies Group (NeuroTech), and the ARTORG Center for Biomedical Engineering Research – as well as with clinical partners at the Inselspital (Bern University Hospital) and with institutions outside the University.
The candidate will work to advance theoretical models of brain information processing, focusing on areas including neuronal activity, synaptic plasticity, machine learning, and the development of fast, energy-efficient neuromorphic systems. The candidate will also play a central role in developing teaching activities in theoretical neuroscience, with a focus on integrating theoretical concepts, neurosciences, and brain-inspired hardware such as neuromorphic devices. The role also involves fostering strong collaboration with experimental and clinical neuroscience groups, including translational research that bridges these domains.
The ideal candidate will be fluent in English and German (learning window possible) and will have a proven track record in teaching, along with the ability to secure funding for interdisciplinary neuroscience research. The candidate should have expertise in fields such as physics, neuroscience, applied mathematics, or related areas, ideally balancing engineering and neuroscience. A strong ability to collaborate across experimental, clinical, and theoretical domains is essential, as well as experience with computational tools relevant to neuroscience and digital medicine. Leadership skills, excellent communication, and the ability to manage diverse, interdisciplinary teams are highly valued. Additionally, the candidate should demonstrate a commitment to diversity, fostering early-career researchers, and promoting inclusive academic practices.

## Self-conception
The University of Bern strives to increase the proportion of women in leadership positions. Women are therefore particularly encouraged to apply. Also, the University of Bern welcomes job-sharing applications. The University of Bern offers support for parents and flexible working time models. Further information can be obtained at Work-life-balance (see job-sharing requirements for more information, https://www.vereinbarkeit.unibe.ch/index_eng.html).
International reputation
Application and Contact
Applications must be submitted solely electronically no later than 2 October 2026 to the Dean's Office of the Medical Faculty of the University of Bern by this link
https://www.recruiting.medizin.unibe.ch/position/14352389
Further information regarding required documentation can be found under https://www.medizin.unibe.ch/research/academic_career_paths/professorship/index_eng.html#pane1397223
or under https://kdrive.medicinebern.ch/app/share/991093/bc77beab-f75a-4634-bbeb-487240307ec0
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About us
The University of Bern, with the generous support of the Manfred Stärk Foundation for Brain Research, is pleased to announce the creation of the Manfred Stärk Professorship for Neuromorphic Systems – a tenure-track Assistant Professor position to be based at the Institute of Physiology, Faculty of Medicine, in Bern, Switzerland.
This newly established position will focus on neuromorphic systems, an interdisciplinary field at the intersection of computational neuroscience, neuroscience, and engineering.
Neuromorphic systems aim to develop circuits and hardware that replicate the self-organizing and self-regulating properties of the brain, with potential applications ranging from medical implants (e.g., for damaged retinas) to autonomous robotics and real-time data processing technologies.
The endowed position will strengthen the University of Bern's research in theoretical neuroscience, aligning with the institution's ongoing contributions to the European Human Brain Project and beyond.

UniBE è per eccellenza bernese. Con noi ci si può aspettare una cultura del rispetto e un ambiente di lavoro sano.

Aufgaben: Il candidato di successo sarà responsabile dell'istituzione di un programma di ricerca indipendente nei sistemi neuromorfi, con l'obiettivo di garantire finanziamenti esterni e promuovere la collaborazione interdisciplinare.

Ciò include la collaborazione all'interno della Facoltà di Medicina. come con l'Istituto di Fisiologia, il Centro di Neurologia Sperimentale (ZEN), il Gruppo Neurotecnologies Neurotecnologiche e il Centro ARTORG per la Ricerca di Ingegneria Biomedica. così come con i partner clinici presso l'Inselpital (Ospedale Universitario di Bern) e con istituzioni esterne all'Università.

Il candidato lavorerà per far progredire modelli teorici di elaborazione delle informazioni cerebrali, concentrandosi su aree quali l'attività neuronale, la plasticità sinaptica, l'apprendimento automatico e lo sviluppo di sistemi neuromorfi veloci ed efficienti in termini energetici. Il candidato svolgerà inoltre un ruolo centrale nello sviluppo di attività didattiche in neuroscienze teoriche, con un focus sull'integrazione di concetti teorici, neuroscienze e hardware di ispirazione cerebrale come dispositivi neuromorfici.

Il ruolo consiste anche nel promuovere una forte collaborazione con gruppi di neuroscienze sperimentali e cliniche, compresa la ricerca traslazionale che collega questi domini.

Il candidato ideale sarà fluente in inglese e tedesco (learning window possibile) e avrà un record di esperienza nell'insegnamento, con la capacità di garantire finanziamenti per la ricerca interdisciplinare sulle neuroscienze. Il candidato dovrebbe avere competenze in campi come la fisica, neuroscienze, matematica applicata, o aree correlate, idealmente bilanciare ingegneria e neuroscienze. Una forte capacità di collaborare in ambiti sperimentali, clinici e teorici è essenziale, così come l'esperienza con strumenti computazionali rilevanti per neuroscienze e medicina digitale.

Le competenze di leadership, l'eccellente comunicazione e la capacità di gestire diversi team interdisciplinare sono molto apprezzate. Inoltre, il candidato dovrebbe dimostrare un impegno verso la diversità, promuovendo ricercatori che si occupano di carriera precoce e promuovendo pratiche accademiche inclusive.

L'Università di Berna offre sostegno ai genitori e modelli flessibili di orario di lavoro. Ulteriori informazioni possono essere ottenute presso il Work-life-balance (cfr. requisiti di condivisione del lavoro per ulteriori informazioni, https://www.vereinbarkeit.unibe.ch/index_eng.html).

jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## Background and objectives
Dietary intake of arsenobetaine (AsB), the dominant arsenic (As) species in fish & seafood, is usually considered harmless due to negligible metabolism and rapid excretion. However, the team leading this project showed in a recent gnotobiotic mouse study that AsB can undergo microbiota-dependent transformations, producing toxic As species. Unfortunately, the extent to which these observations are translatable to humans remains as of today unresolved. Clarifying this question is toxicologically important, as even small AsB conversion to more toxic As species would be relevant for risk assessment.
In this project we aim to determine human gut microbiota mediated AsB transformations using a range of liquid chromatography speciation methods to quantify conversion rates of AsB into toxic As species under relevant exposure conditions and to assess interindividual variability. The hired postdoc will use in vitro human fecal microbiota assays from various donors to establish translational relevance. The results will directly support FSVO/EFSA in evaluating whether AsB-rich seafood may constitute a yet unrecognized source of toxic As species in humans.

## Your tasks and our expectations
• Establish robust analytical methods to determine AsB transformation in fecal microbiota: extraction from samples as well as method validation for a range of arsenic speciation methods using HPLC-ICP-MS/MS
• Establish robust experimental designs
• Culture human fecal microbiota from ongoing cohort studies (e.g. BeBiCo on the development of the infant microbiome)
• Screen AsB transformation in these cultures
• Test realistic exposure scenarios and explore microbial determinants
• Reporting, paper writing, scientific presentations
• Participate in HPLC-ICP-MS troubleshooting among other tasks in the laboratory
The successful candidate should hold a PhD degree in Environmental or Analytical Chemistry or related field and have proven research experience in using hyphenated method. Independent use of HPLC-ICP-MS to measure trace element species in matrices other than water is a must. Someone with experience on arsenic speciation would be preferred. The successful candidate should have excellent English writing and communication skills and a proven track record of scientific presentations and publications. Other essentials skills include a strong team orientation, working in a precise, engaged and self-organized manner as well as commitment to work in an interdisciplinary field with multiple supervisors.
Specific experience in the following domains would be an asset:
• Statistics and data visualisation,
• Method development and/or troubleshooting in HPLC-ICP-MS,
• Microbiology
• Incubations.
International reputation
Application and Contact
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About us and the project
We are looking for a motivated early-postdoc (< 3 years post PhD) with analytical and environmental chemistry experience interested in being part of our interdisciplinary project titled “Microbial Degradation of Arsenobetaine in the Human Gut: Implications for Dietary Arsenic Exposure and Risk Assessment.” The project is led by an interfaculty team composed of Prof. Dr. Adrien Mestrot (GIUB, Soil Biogeochemistry, Inorganic Environmental Chemistry), Prof. Dr. Siegfried Hapfelmeier (IFIK, Gut microbiology) and Prof. Dr. Stephanie Ganal-Vonarbrug (DBMR, Immunology, Microbiology). The project will take full advantage of the state-of-the-art facilities present at our institutes (e.g. cLab of the GIUB with HPLC-ICP-MS instruments, anaerobic incubators at IFIK and DBMR) and will rely on ongoing human cohort studies to secure samples. It is funded by and run in close collaboration with the Federal Office for Food Safety and Veterinary Affairs.

L'assunzione dietetica di arsenobetaina (AsB), la specie arsenica dominante (As) nel pesce e nei frutti di mare, è generalmente considerata innocua a causa del metabolismo trascurabile e dell'escrezione rapida. Tuttavia, il team leader di questo progetto ha mostrato in un recente studio del mouse gnotobiotico che AsB può subire trasformazioni microbiota-dipendenti, producendo come specie tossiche. Purtroppo, la misura in cui queste osservazioni sono traducibili agli esseri umani rimane oggi irrisolta. Chiarificare questa domanda è tossicologicamente importante, come anche la piccola conversione AsB a più tossico Poiché le specie sarebbero rilevanti per la valutazione del rischio.
In questo progetto si mira a determinare le trasformazioni di microbiota dell'intestino umano mediate AsB utilizzando una gamma di metodi di speciazione della cromatografia liquida per quantificare i tassi di conversione di AsB in tossico Come specie in condizioni di esposizione pertinenti e valutare la variabilità interindividuale. Il postdoc assunto utilizzerà in vitro analisi microbiota fecali umane da vari donatori per stabilire rilevanza traduttiva. I risultati sosterranno direttamente l'FSVO/EFSA per valutare se i frutti di mare ricchi di AsB possano costituire una fonte ancora non riconosciuta di sostanze tossiche Come specie negli esseri umani.

Anforderungen:

• Stabilire robusti disegni sperimentali

Il candidato di successo dovrebbe avere eccellenti capacità di scrittura e comunicazione inglese e una comprovata traccia record di presentazioni e pubblicazioni scientifiche. ## Job description
This PhD project is part of Workpackage 3 of NCCR CLIM+, which concentrates on questions of governance and justice around the regulation of climate extremes (such as droughts, floods, heatwaves, and heavy precipitation amongst others). The successful candidate will complete a PhD thesis at the interface of law and political science. Specifically, the thesis will investigate under what conditions law and politics recognize and define an event as 'extreme' and what this means for resulting goveranance responses and questions of justice.

• Interest in exploring the governance of extreme climate events at the intersection of law and political science
• Curious, creative and comfortable working in interdisciplinary settings

jobs.description:
Die UniBE ist vernetzt.
Bei uns sind Sie Teil einer internationalen Gemeinschaft und profitieren von der interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit.

## Ihre Aufgaben
• Sie bearbeiten und entwickeln eigenständig Forschungsfragen im Bereich Suizidalität und Suizidprävention weiter
• Sie koordinieren und entwickeln laufende Forschungsprojekte weiter
• Sie planen und führen Studien sowie statistische Analysen durch
• Sie erstellen und publizieren wissenschaftliche Manuskripte
• Sie wirken bei Drittmittelanträgen und Forschungskooperationen mit
• Sie präsentieren Forschungsergebnisse auf nationalen und internationalen Kongressen
• Sie wirken in der Lehre und bei der Betreuung von Studierenden mit
• Sie tragen aktiv zur wissenschaftlichen Weiterentwicklung der Forschungsgruppe bei

## Ihr Profil
• Sie verfügen über ein abgeschlossenes Doktorat (PhD/Dr.) in Psychologie, Neurowissenschaften oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet
• Sie bringen Erfahrung in der Planung, Durchführung und Auswertung empirischer Forschungsprojekte mit
• Sie verfügen über sehr gute Kenntnisse in quantitativen Forschungsmethoden und Statistik
• Sie haben Erfahrung mit wissenschaftlichen Publikationen
• Sie interessieren sich für klinische Forschung, insbesondere im Bereich Suizidalität und Suizidprävention
• Sie möchten eigene Forschungsfragen entwickeln und Ihr wissenschaftliches Profil weiterentwickeln
• Sie verfügen über sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse
• Sie arbeiten selbstständig, strukturiert und zuverlässig
• Sie arbeiten gerne interdisziplinär und international
• Erfahrungen in der Suizidforschung, klinischen Forschung, EMA, digitalen oder psychophysiologischen Messmethoden sind von Vorteil
Internationales Renommee
Bewerbung und Kontakt
Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbungsunterlagen über den Button "Bewerben".
Bei uns schaffen Sie Wert.
Für sich und die Gesellschaft.

## Über uns
Interessieren Sie sich für klinische und neurowissenschaftliche Fragestellungen im Bereich Suizidalität und Suizidprävention? Möchten Sie Ihre wissenschaftliche Karriere in einem interdisziplinären Forschungsumfeld weiterentwickeln und einen Beitrag zum besseren Verständnis und zur Behandlung von Menschen mit suizidalem Erleben und Verhalten leisten?
Die multidisziplinäre Forschungsgruppe von PD Dr. phil. Anja Gysin-Maillart und Prof. Dr. med. Kristina Adorjan an der Universitätsklinik für Erwachsenenpsychiatrie und Psychotherapie Bern beschäftigt sich mit der Früherkennung, dem Verständnis und der Behandlung von suizidalem Erleben und Verhalten im Erwachsenenalter. Unsere Forschung verbindet klinische Fragestellungen mit empirischen und neurowissenschaftlichen Methoden wie klinischen Interviews, Fragebögen, neuropsychologischen Verfahren, Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) sowie digitalen und physiologischen Messmethoden.
Zur Verstärkung suchen wir einen engagierten Postdoc, der/die sein/ihr wissenschaftliches Profil weiterentwickeln und eigenständige Forschungsprojekte im Bereich Suizidforschung und Suizidprävention gestalten möchte. Wir bieten eine wissenschaftlich anspruchsvolle Position in einem interdisziplinären Umfeld mit Möglichkeiten zur Entwicklung eigener Forschungsprojekte, Unterstützung bei Publikationen und Drittmittelanträgen, Zugang zu bestehenden Forschungsprojekten und Datensätzen sowie nationaler und internationaler Vernetzung. Zudem profitieren Sie von Mentoring, Weiterbildungs- und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten sowie der Teilnahme an wissenschaftlichen Kongressen.

jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## 
• Profile
We are looking for a creative and motivated candidate, a team player, with a MSc degree in physics, chemistry, or biology. Willingness to learn microbiological techniques is essential; prior wet lab experience is an asset. No prior expertise in optics is required; training will be provided, though a basic understanding of polarization, vacuum technology and/or mass spectrometry is a plus. Excellent oral and written skills in English are a requirement.

## 
• What we offer
The position is based at the Centre for Space and Habitability, which strives to investigate key questions in space sciences through interdisciplinarity. The team collaborates tightly with various national and international partners. This includes for example the Microbiology Laboratory of the University of Neuchâtel where the lab measurements on microorganisms will be conducted. Laser-based mass spectrometry on organics will be conducted at the Space Research and Planetary Sciences division of the University of Bern, which is closely collaborating with colleagues at NASA Ames Research Center, USA.
The city of Bern is well known for its quality of life, cultural richness and beautiful surroundings offering plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities.
The position is funded for a period of 4 years. The annual gross salary is competitive, ranging from CHF 50,042 in the first year to CHF 53,263 in the final year. Ample funding for travel, publications and computing resources will be available. Child allowance and maternity/paternity leave are offered. Assistance with visa procedures is available for international candidates. Additionally, the CSH offers career advice, mentorship, and teaching opportunities.
International reputation
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## NCCR Genesis: background
The Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) and the Division for Space Research and Planetary Sciences (WP) at the University of Bern invite applications for a PhD position in the frame of the new NCCR Genesis.
The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect unambiguous traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.
Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch.
Our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion
NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.
Project description
Are we alone in the universe? The search for life beyond the Earth is one of the most fascinating endeavours that humankind has embarked upon. Recent years have seen tremendous progress in instrumentation, laboratory experiments and theories on the origin of life.
This PhD project will investigate for the first time the combination of remote life sensing techniques using circular spectro-polarimetry with in situ laser-based mass spectrometry measurements, both designed for the detection or signatures of life. The work will mainly involve experiments in the lab, using cell cultures of a range of strains (including anaerobic cultivation of microorganisms) and various classes of organic molecules relevant to Solar System environments. These studies will be complemented by targeted field measurements of soil material containing microorganisms and low abundant organics that are relevant candidates for extinct/extant life on Mars or in the icy moons of the solar system. The results of this endeavour will reveal the potential of combining life detection methods at different scales that will be key to define optimal strategies for future life-detection missions, such as the planned ESA L4 mission to Enceladus or future NASA mission to Mars.
The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team with expertise spanning astrophysics, microbiology, biomedicine and engineering. The new group member will have the opportunity to gain unique experience in dual-use instrumentation applicable to both space exploration and medical diagnostics.

UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## 
• Profile
We are looking for a creative and motivated candidate, a team player, with a MSc degree in physics or engineering. Prior expertise in optics is an asset and a basic understanding of polarisation is a plus. Excellent oral and written skills in English are a requirement.

## 
• What we offer
The position is based at the Centre for Space and Habitability, which strives to investigate key questions in space sciences through interdisciplinarity. Our team collaborates tightly with the Microbiology Laboratory (Prof. Pilar Junier) of the University of Neuchâtel where the lab measurements are conducted. The city of Bern is well known for its quality of life, cultural richness and beautiful surroundings offering plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities.
The position is funded for a period of 4 years. The annual gross salary is competitive, ranging from CHF 50,042 in the first year to CHF 53,263 in the final year. Ample funding for travel, publications and computing resources will be available. Child allowance and maternity/paternity leave are offered. Assistance with visa procedures is available for international candidates. Additionally, the CSH offers career advice, mentorship, and teaching opportunities.
International reputation
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## NCCR Genesis: background
The Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) at the University of Bern invites applications for a PhD position in the frame of the new NCCR Genesis.
The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect unambiguous traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.
Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch.
Our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion
NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.
Project description
Are we alone in the universe? The search for life beyond the Earth is one of the most fascinating endeavours that humankind has embarked upon. Recent years have seen tremendous progress in instrumentation, laboratory experiments and theories on the origin of life.
This PhD project will investigate the impact of icy-moon environmental conditions on the detectability of selected bacteria in ice/salt mixtures rapidly exposed to vacuum, extremely low temperatures and high-radiation levels. For this purpose, a high-sensitivity spectro-polarimeter will be interfaced with a temperature-vacuum chamber. Additionally, an electron gun and a UV light source will be used to investigate the incidence of harsh conditions on bacterial samples deposited on ice as a proxy for icy moon conditions. The study will also investigate whether spectro-polarimetry could probe fundamental structures in the microorganisms such as cofactors or proteins in the near UV. The project will thus investigate the detectability of fundamental biosignatures relevant to a wider range of microorganisms. This effort will inform the preparation of future life-detection missions in our Solar System, such as the planned ESA L4 mission to Enceladus.
The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team (lead: Prof. Brice-Olivier Demory) with expertise spanning astrophysics, microbiology, biomedicine and engineering. The new group member will have the opportunity to gain unique experience in dual-use instrumentation applicable to both space exploration and medical diagnostics.

jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## Research and Collaborative Environment
The PhD student will be hosted at the Institute of Mathematical Statistics and Actuarial Science (IMSV) of the University of Bern, joining the Uncertainty Quantification and Spatial Statistics group led by Prof. David Ginsbourger. The IMSV is an engaged, open-minded institute where mathematical statistics and probability theory meet data and models arising from various scientific and societal challenges
The position is part of the NCCR CLIM+ programme on Climate Extremes and Society, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). More specifically, the PhD project will contribute to the work package “Local Risks: Impacts and Adaptation” and involve participation in tasks covering topics such as the downscaling and debiasing of input data for hydrological models. Regular interactions and potential collaborations with the teams of Prof. Manuela Brunner (ETH Zurich, WSL), Dr. Christian Grams (MeteoSwiss), Prof. Michael Lehning (EPFL Valais Wallis, WSL), and Prof. Olivia Romppainen-Martius (University of Bern) are planned.
The NCCR CLIM+ supports Switzerland in the transformation towards a climate-resilient society. Together with stakeholders, the interdisciplinary NCCR CLIM+ research community tackles unexplored solution spaces to the climate crisis and develops a blueprint for actionable climate research worldwide. NCCR CLIM+ broadly communicates and shares knowledge, and trains a new generation of experts with the necessary domain and transdisciplinary knowledge.
The NCCR CLIM+ strives to implement equal opportunity at hiring. At NCCR CLIM+ we believe that diversity of thought, background and experience creates better research.

## Profile of the candidate
• A MSc degree in statistics or a closely related field with strong mathematical background
• Strong programming skills (ideally in Python and/or R)
• Knowledge and ideally practical experience of generative machine learning
• Experience in working with large datasets, ideally hydrological, meteorological or climate observations/simulations
• Very good oral and written communication skills in English
• Motivation to work in an interdisciplinary and international working environment and a collaborative mindset
International reputation
Application and Contact
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following elements:
• your CV,
• a cover letter,
• diploma certificates and transcripts,
• a link to your MSc thesis (draft or final version),
• and the contact information of two professional references.
Applications submitted by October 1, 2026 (inclusive) are guaranteed full consideration.

## About the project
We invite applications for a PhD position in Statistics focusing on conditional generative modelling of local high-impact events in a changing climate. Generative models are increasingly used in weather forecasting and climate research, notably to downscale global predictions and projections to local scales. Their use for studying future high-impact events raises fundamental statistical and computational challenges, including the integration of heterogeneous data sources, conditioning on complex information, and generalisation to climate conditions beyond those represented in the training data.
In this PhD project, we will investigate existing and develop new conditional generative modelling approaches for studying future high-impact events at local scales under prescribed, structured conditioning scenarios. These may include large-scale dynamical storylines and event-prone regimes. The project will address methodological questions in conditional generation, the representation and integration of conditioning information, and the generation of plausible local outcomes under changing and potentially unprecedented climate conditions.

## About the project
We invite applications for a PhD position in Statistics focusing on conditional generative modelling of local high-impact events in a changing climate. Generative models are increasingly used in weather forecasting and climate research, notably to downscale global predictions and projections to local scales. Their use for studying future high-impact events raises fundamental statistical and computational challenges, including the integration of heterogeneous data sources, conditioning on complex information, and generalisation to climate conditions beyond those represented in the training data.
In this PhD project, we will investigate existing and develop new conditional generative modelling approaches for studying future high-impact events at local scales under prescribed, structured conditioning scenarios. These may include large-scale dynamical storylines and event-prone regimes. L'IMSV est un institut engagé et ouvert d'esprit où les statistiques mathématiques et la théorie des probabilités rencontrent les données et les modèles découlant de divers défis scientifiques et sociétaux Ce poste fait partie du programme CNCR CLIM+ sur les extrêmes climatiques et la société, financé par la Fondation nationale suisse de la science (SNSF). Plus précisément, le projet de doctorat contribuera à l'ensemble de travail "Risques locaux: impacts et adaptation" et implique la participation à des tâches couvrant des sujets tels que la réduction de l'échelle et la décomposition des données d'entrée pour les modèles hydrologiques. Des interactions régulières et des collaborations potentielles avec les équipes du Prof. Manuela Brunner (ETH Zurich, WSL), du Dr. Christian Grams (MeteoSwiss), du Prof. Michael Lehning (EPFL Valais Wallis, WSL) et du Prof. Olivia Romppainen-Martius (Université de Berne) sont prévues. Le CCNR CLIM+ soutient la Suisse dans sa transformation vers une société résiliente au climat. En collaboration avec les parties prenantes, la communauté de recherche interdisciplinaire NCCR CLIM+ s'attaque aux espaces de solutions inexplorés à la crise climatique et élabore un plan de recherche sur le climat à l'échelle mondiale. Le CCNR CLIM+ communique et partage largement ses connaissances et forme une nouvelle génération d'experts possédant les connaissances transdisciplinaires et de domaine nécessaires. Le CCNR CLIM+ s'efforce de mettre en oeuvre l'égalité des chances en matière d'embauche. UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## Research and Collaborative Environment
The PhD student will be hosted at the Institute of Mathematical Statistics and Actuarial Science (IMSV) of the University of Bern, joining the Uncertainty Quantification and Spatial Statistics group led by Prof. David Ginsbourger. IMSV is an engaged, open-minded institute where mathematical statistics and probability theory meet data and models arising from various scientific and societal challenges.
The position is part of the NCCR CLIM+ programme on Climate Extremes and Society, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). More specifically, the PhD project will contribute to the work package “Local Risks: Impacts and Adaptation” and involve participation in tasks covering topics such as the downscaling and debiasing of input data for hydrological models. Regular interactions and potential collaborations with the teams of Prof. Manuela Brunner (ETH Zurich, WSL), Dr. Christian Grams (MeteoSwiss), Prof. Michael Lehning (EPFL Valais Wallis, WSL), and Prof. Olivia Romppainen-Martius (University of Bern) are planned.
The NCCR CLIM+ supports Switzerland in the transformation towards a climate-resilient society. Together with stakeholders, the interdisciplinary NCCR CLIM+ research community tackles unexplored solution spaces to the climate crisis and develops a blueprint for actionable climate research worldwide. NCCR CLIM+ broadly communicates and shares knowledge, and trains a new generation of experts with the necessary domain and transdisciplinary knowledge.
The NCCR CLIM+ strives to implement equal opportunity at hiring. At NCCR CLIM+ we believe that diversity of thought, background and experience creates better research

## Profile of the candidate
• A MSc degree in statistics or a closely related field with strong mathematical background
• Strong programming skills (ideally in Python and/or R)
• Knowledge and ideally practical experience of generative machine learning
• Experience in working with large datasets, ideally hydrological, meteorological or climate observations/simulations
• Very good oral and written communication skills in English
• Motivation to work in an interdisciplinary and international working environment and a collaborative mindset
International reputation
Application and Contact
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following elements:
• your CV,
• a cover letter,
• diploma certificates and transcripts,
• a link to your MSc thesis (draft or final version),
• and the contact information of two professional references.
Applications submitted by October 1, 2026 (inclusive) are guaranteed full consideration.

## About the project
We invite applications for a PhD position in Statistics focusing on conditional generative modelling of local high-impact events in a changing climate. Generative models are increasingly used in weather forecasting and climate research, notably to downscale global predictions and projections to local scales. Their use for studying future high-impact events raises fundamental statistical and computational challenges, including the integration of heterogeneous data sources, conditioning on complex information, and generalisation to climate conditions beyond those represented in the training data.
In this PhD project, we will investigate existing and develop new conditional generative modelling approaches for studying future high-impact events at local scales under prescribed, structured conditioning scenarios. These may include large-scale dynamical storylines and event-prone regimes. The project will address methodological questions in conditional generation, the representation and integration of conditioning information, and the generation of plausible local outcomes under changing and potentially unprecedented climate conditions.
Research and Collaborative Environment

jobs.description:
Die UniBE ist typisch Bern.
Bei uns erwartet Sie eine wertschätzende Kultur und ein gesundes Arbeitsklima.

Als Teil des Kaufmännischen Gebäudemanagements verbinden Sie Immobilienmanagement, Administration und Controlling. jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## 
• Job description
The aim of the thesis is to further develop multi-variable, high-resolution daily weather reconstructions for Switzerland and Europe and to analyse the historical frequency, intensity, characteristics and timing of past weather and climate extremes in these data. The focus will be on heatwaves, droughts, wildfires and floods. Alongside statistical analysis, the meteorological and climatological conditions that lead to climate extremes will be studied, as well as the impact of these events in the past. The goal is to quantify the variability of weather and climate extremes in the pre-industrial era using multi-century observation-based meteorological fields alongside climate model simulations. The thesis will inform the generation of storylines of climate extreme and contribute to attribution studies within the project.

## 
• Your profile
We are looking for a candidate with an MSc degree in geography, climate science, environmental science or similar, with proven skills in statistics, quantitative methods and programming as well as openness for interdisciplinary work. The University of Bern promotes equal opportunity and diversity, supporting female and minority researchers.

Bei uns liefern Sie Spitzenleistungen und testen Ihre Fähigkeiten gegen die Besten. Aufgaben: Ziel der Arbeit ist es, multivariable, hochauflösende tägliche Wetterrekonstruktionen für die Schweiz und Europa weiterzuentwickeln und in diesen Daten die historische Häufigkeit, Intensität, Charakteristik und das Timing vergangener Wetter- und Klimaextreme zu analysieren. Im Fokus stehen Hitzewellen, Dürren, Waldbrände und Überschwemmungen. Neben der statistischen Analyse werden die meteorologischen und klimatischen Bedingungen, die zu Klimaextremen führen, sowie die Auswirkungen dieser Ereignisse in der Vergangenheit untersucht. Ziel ist es, die Variabilität von Wetter- und Klimaextremen in der vorindustriellen Ära unter Verwendung von meteorologischen Beobachtungsfeldern aus mehreren Jahrhunderten neben Klimamodellsimulationen zu quantifizieren. Die Arbeit wird die Generierung von Handlungssträngen des Klimaextrems informieren und zu Attributionsstudien innerhalb des Projekts beitragen. Anforderungen: Wir suchen einen Kandidaten mit einem MSc-Abschluss in Geographie, Klimawissenschaft, Umweltwissenschaften oder ähnlichem, mit nachgewiesenen Fähigkeiten in Statistik, quantitativen Methoden und Programmierung sowie Offenheit für interdisziplinäres Arbeiten. Die Universität Bern fördert Chancengleichheit und Diversität und unterstützt Forscherinnen und Forscher aus Minderheiten. Wir bieten: Internationale Reputation

jobs.title: Postdoc PROTECT-SH und NASA
jobs.description:
Die UniBE ist vernetzt.
Bei uns sind Sie Teil einer internationalen Gemeinschaft und profitieren von der interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit.

## Deine Aufgaben
• Du unterstützt die Koordination des multizentrischen Projekts PROTECT-SH vom Koordinationsstandort Bern aus
• Du konzipierst drei grosse randomisiert-kontrollierte Studien aktiv mit und übernimmst Aufgaben im Bereich Datenmanagement und Panelpflege
• Du beteiligst dich an Entwicklung und Evaluation digitaler Interventionen (z.B. Apps, EMA/EMI) zur Prävention von Selbstverletzung und Suizidalität
• Du wertest quantitative Daten aus, verfasst wissenschaftliche Publikationen und präsentierst Ergebnisse an nationalen und internationalen Kongressen
• Du betreust Doktorierende und Masterstudierende mit

## Dein Profil
• Du verfügst über eine abgeschlossene Promotion in Psychologie oder einem verwandten Fach
• Du hast Erfahrung in der Planung und Durchführung klinischer Studien
• Du bringst fundierte Kenntnisse statistischer Verfahren und Erfahrungen mit deren Anwendung (z.B. mit R, Stata, Mplus) mit
• Erfahrung mit digitalen Erhebungs- oder Interventionsmethoden (z.B. EMA, App-basierte Interventionen, digitale Phänotypisierung) ist von Vorteil
• Du kommunizierst souverän mit internationalen Projektpartner*innen und die Arbeit mit jungen Menschen macht dir Freude
• Du hast gleichermassen Freude an eigenständigem Arbeiten und der Zusammenarbeit im Team
• Du hast sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse
Internationales Renommee
Bewerbung und Kontakt
Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung über den Button "Bewerben".
Bei uns schaffen Sie Wert.
Für sich und die Gesellschaft.

## Über uns
Die ausgeschriebene Stelle beinhaltet die Mitarbeit in zwei grossen Forschungsprojekten zum übergeordneten Thema «Self-Harm and New Media».
Ein Teil der Arbeit erfolgt im Rahmen von PROTECT-SH, einem durch Horizon Europe geförderten Verbundprojekt mit Partnern in sieben Ländern. PROTECT-SH untersucht über vier Jahre in einer multizentrischen Längsschnittkohorte, über welche Mechanismen die Nutzung sozialer Medien selbstverletzendes und suizidales Verhalten bei Jugendlichen und jungen Erwachsenen fördert oder davor schützt. Darauf aufbauend wird eine digitale Intervention in zwei grossen randomisiert-kontrollierten Studien (Prävention und klinische Intervention) entwickelt und evaluiert. Du übernimmst im Verbund eine koordinierende Rolle und unterstützt von den Ethik- und Studienunterlagen bis zur Durchführung und Auswertung der beiden Studien.
Das zweite Projekt, NASA, beinhaltet die Implementierung und wissenschaftlichen Evaluation einer App zur Suizidprävention innerhalb unserer Klinik, ebenfalls im randomisiert-kontrollierten Design. Zusätzlich gibt es die Möglichkeit an weiteren internen Projekten unserer Arbeitsgruppe im Bereich Selbstverletzung und Suizidalität mitzuwirken sowie bereits vorhandenen Datensätze auszuwerten und zu publizieren.
Die Stelle eignet sich für Kandidatinnen und Kandidaten in der frühen Postdoc-Phase, die ein grosses internationales Forschungsprojekt aktiv mitgestalten möchten. Wir arbeiten eng im Team zusammen und sind interdisziplinär und international vernetzt. Weitere Informationen zu unserer Forschungsabteilung
Die Stelle ist zunächst auf 2 Jahre befristet, mit Option auf Verlängerung im Rahmen der Projektlaufzeit und auch darüber hinaus bei besonderer Eignung. Die Entlohnung erfolgt gemäss den Richtlinien der Universität Bern.

jobs.description:
Die UniBE ist mittendrin.
Bei uns profitieren Sie von der zentralen Lage und verkehrstechnisch günstig gelegenen Standorten.

## Aufgaben
• First-Level-Support und Help Desk inklusive Entgegennahme, Priorisierung, Analyse und Bearbeitung von IT-Anfragen sowie Eskalation komplexerer Störungen
• Beratung und Unterstützung der Mitarbeitenden bei Fragen zu ICT-Services und Arbeitsplatzsystemen
• Installation, Konfiguration, Betrieb und Unterhalt von Windows-Clients, Notebooks, Druckern, Peripherie- und Netzwerkgeräten
• Administration ausgewählter Windows-Server, Services, Active Directory sowie grundlegender Netzwerkdienste wie DNS, DHCP und TCP/IP
• Mitarbeit beim Patch- und Update-Management, insbesondere mit WSUS, sowie Überwachung von Datensicherungen und Unterstützung bei Wiederherstellungen
• Technische Betreuung von Laborarbeitsplätzen, Steuerungssystemen und weiteren institutsspezifischen IT-Systemen
• Unterstützung bei Umzügen, Inbetriebnahmen sowie der Übernahme neuer oder geänderter Hard- und Software in den Betrieb
• Mitarbeit bei IT-Projekten und bei der Einführung und Weiterentwicklung von ICT-Systemen
• Erstellung und Pflege von technischen Dokumentationen, Inventaren und Anwenderanleitungen sowie Durchführung von Anwenderschulungen
• Unterstützung bei Beschaffung und Verwaltung von IT-Hardware, Software und Verbrauchsmaterial
• Betreuung ausgewählter Spezial- und Websysteme sowie Teilnahme am IT-Pikettdienst
• Einhaltung der geltenden Reglemente, Weisungen und Sicherheitsrichtlinien

## Anforderungen
• Abgeschlossene Berufsausbildung als Informatiker, vorzugsweise mit Schwerpunkt Systemtechnik beziehungsweise Plattformentwicklung, oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung
• Berufserfahrung im IT-Support sowie in der Administration von Windows-Systemen
• Gute Kenntnisse in den Bereichen Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Gruppenrichtlinien und TCP/IP
• Erfahrung mit Windows-Clients und Microsoft-Office-Umgebungen
• Kenntnisse in der Administration von Windows-Servern und im Patch-Management
• Grundkenntnisse im Bereich Netzwerk, Datensicherung und IT-Sicherheit
• Erfahrung im Umgang mit Ticketsystemen und strukturierten Supportprozessen von Vorteil
• Selbstständige, zuverlässige und serviceorientierte Arbeitsweise
• Selbstständige, strukturierte und dienstleistungsorientierte Arbeitsweise
• Hohes Qualitäts- und Sicherheitsbewusstsein
• Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift
Interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit
Bewerbung und Kontakt
Bei uns schaffen Sie Wert.
Für sich und die Gesellschaft.

## Über uns
Das Institut für Infektionskrankheiten nimmt Aufgaben in der Mikrobiologie in den Fachrichtungen Virologie, Bakteriologie, Mykologie, Parasitologie und serologischer Infektionsabklärung wahr. Mit 200 Mitarbeitenden vereint es als einziges universitäres Institut der Schweiz alle mikrobiologischen Spezialdisziplinen in der Forschung, Lehre und Diagnostik unter einem Dach.
Das IFIK ist auch Sitz des Nationalen Referenzzentrums für Pneumokokken (NZPn) und des Nationalen Zentrums für Antibiotikaresistenz (anresis.ch) im Auftrag des Bundesamtes für Gesundheit. Unser Biosicherheitszentrum ist ein Kollaborationscenter der World Health Organisation (WHO).
Wollen Sie in einem dynamischen Umfeld tätig sein, in dem Teamarbeit geschätzt wird und Zusammenhalt zählt? Wenn Sie offen, motiviert und bereit sind, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, freuen wir uns darauf, Sie kennenzulernen. Bewerben Sie sich jetzt und werden Sie Teil unseres engagierten Teams.
